name: repository redirection is left in the environment
edits:
for var in REDIRECT_VARS:
        out.pop(var, None)
expect: git -C means what it says: GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_COMMON_DIR are removed

name: the throwaway index variable is stripped along with the redirections
expect: …GIT_INDEX_FILE is KEPT, because reviewed_state sets it on purpose

name: a null dirty map is collapsed into an empty one in the record
edits: "dirty": None if dirty is None else dict(dirty),
expect: a null dirty map survives into the record as null, not as an empty map

name: the prompt the run was dispatched with is dropped
expect: the verdict records the prompt the run was dispatched with

name: a deletion is skipped rather than recorded
edits:
if set(parts[3]) == {"0"}:
            continue
        dirty[path] = f"{parts[1]} {parts[3]}"
    return head.strip(), dirty
expect: …and a DELETED file is recorded as the all-zero entry, not skipped

name: the SOURCE mode is recorded instead of the destination mode
expect: …and the UNTRACKED one too, at its DESTINATION mode, not the 000000 source mode

name: the throwaway index is abandoned, so the repository's own index is used
expect: the repository's own index is untouched — the staging went to a throwaway one

name: every tracked file is recorded, changed or not
expect: a file identical to HEAD is not recorded as handed over

name: a wrapper with no head claims a clean tree instead of saying it could not look
expect: …and says it could not describe the tree with null, not with an empty map

name: the reason is dropped, so the classifier half stops reporting WHY a case failed
expect: the line keeps the canonical shape the harness documents

name: the contract is asserted against a stub instead of the harness's real parser
expect: the FAIL line this suite prints parses back to the case name, via the harness's OWN parser

name: the one FAIL-line shape reverts to got=, so every kill in this file goes unattributable
edits: return f"  [{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {name}: got {got!r} want {want!r}{tail}"
return f"  [{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {name}: got={got!r}{tail}"
expect: the line keeps the canonical shape the harness documents: got=False

name: r5 M1: testimony is written into docs/reviews itself, where halves are scanned
expect: VERDICT_DIR is a SUBdirectory of docs/reviews, which the non-recursive intrusion snapshot and the review-half scan both depend on

name: r5 M3: the floor deciding whether a gate RAN drops to three characters
expect: MIN_REVIEW_CHARS is pinned — the floor that decides whether a gate RAN cannot drift silently

name: r5 L1: the rate limit stops counting as an account-level fault
expect: the account-fault statuses are the three that mean 'later models will fail too'

name: #176: an unclassifiable review id is accepted and filed under a DEFAULT writer
edits:
got = parse_review_name(f"{review_id}.md")
    if got is None:

got = parse_review_name(f"{review_id}.md") or (review_id, 0, "codex")
    if got is None:
expect: an id with NO round number is REFUSED, never filed under the writer it happens to end in

name: #176: the filing grammar is re-implemented privately instead of imported
expect: shape B — `<subject>-<writer>-r<N>` — classifies too, at a DIFFERENT writer, which a private suffix rule cannot do

name: #176: the coordinator counts as a review HALF, so a round passes with one reviewer and its own summary
expect: an id naming the COORDINATOR is refused — it adjudicates the halves and is not one

name: #176: the CI join key drops the extension, so it names no file on disk
expect: ⭐ a failed gate whose review IS filed is reported by the real check-review-rounds, whatever --out was called

name: #176: the filed name and the join key drift apart by one spelling
expect: the verdict names the review it is about, as the filename that review is filed under

name: #176: the promotion writes into the artifact ROOT, where quarantine() moves it back out
expect: the promoted review is filed one level DOWN, under its writer, where the non-recursive intrusion snapshot cannot mistake it for an agent's guess

name: #176: the writer stops selecting the directory, so a claude half is filed under codex
expect: …and the WRITER selects the directory, so a claude half is not filed under codex

name: #176: promote() never asks the filesystem, so the write-time check is the pre-flight's stale answer
expect: promote REFUSES an existing destination rather than replacing it

name: #176: promotion reports success while filing an empty review
edits:
with open(dest, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(body)

with open(dest, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            pass
expect: …and the promoted file holds exactly the captured artifact, byte for byte

name: #176: the retired --verdict flag dies on argparse instead of naming its retirement
expect: …and SAYS it was retired, naming --review-id as what owns the identity now

name: #176: --review-id stops being required, so the identity can go unsupplied again
expect: a missing --review-id is a CANNOT RUN (2), never a fallback to deriving one from --out

name: #176: the overwrite policy stops refusing, so a filed review is replaced silently
expect: an existing artifact is REFUSED by default

name: #176: the overwrite policy refuses a path that is not there, blocking every first run
expect: …and a path that does not exist is never a refusal

name: #176: the --allow-overwrite escape is inverted, so the deliberate replacement is the one refused
expect: …and --allow-overwrite is honoured, so a deliberate replacement is not blocked
